content.title: About
content.content: Bran flakes are a whole‑grain breakfast cereal made from wheat bran. They have a neutral taste, a crunchy texture, and are commonly enjoyed with milk, yogurt, or fruit.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bran is the outer layer of the grain, rich in fiber and nutrients.
Bran flakes are popular in diet plans because of their low calorie density.
Unlike sweet cereals, they contain no added sugar.
Bran can help improve digestion and regulate blood sugar levels.
In some regions they are simply called "bran flakes" or "wheat bran flakes".

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber support gut health and promote satiety.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: The absence of added sugars makes them suitable for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Bran provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium and zinc in bran contribute to blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Fiber helps lower LDL cholesterol, reducing cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: Bran flakes contain gluten and should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Excess fiber
items.content: Large servings may cause bloating, gas, or diarrhea in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in very high amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Typically pour milk or a plant‑based beverage over the flakes, add fresh or dried fruit, nuts, honey, or yogurt. They can also be used as a base for granola bars or incorporated into baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For extended shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
